researched_by: the council's car park pages and off-street order amendments, council news releases, and press/forum corroboration
policy_summary:
Zero provision, and a quietly systematic lockout. Dorset Council admits motorhomes by day in 31 of its 80-plus car parks, with separate tariffs for under and over 6 metres (over-6m 'multiuse' rates run to GBP30-plus a day, GBP90 a week), but the off-street parking order bars motorhomes from those same car parks between 10pm and 8am. The clause appears car park by car park - confirmed at Chesil (Portland), West Bay Road, Lodmoor (Weymouth) and Charmouth Road (Lyme Regis) - and Amendment No. 3 (January 2025) added it to Stour Meadows (Blandford) and Southill (Weymouth), so the net is still being extended. The council's public line, given in June 2022 after overnight sleeping at Weymouth's Pavilion car park, was that 'overnight sleeping is not permitted as car parks are not designed as campsites'; it said then that it was investigating motorhome provision and talking to CAMpRA. Four years on, nothing has appeared.

The Jurassic Coast pressure points are held shut by other hands too. Durdle Door and Lulworth Cove are Lulworth Estate land: the Durdle Door car park is gated 8am-9pm, charges motorhomes GBP30 for the day with the tariff itself marked 'NO OVERNIGHT SLEEPING', and runs ANPR. At West Bay, Station Yard is now signed no-motorhomes altogether and West Bay Road (motorhome bays, 6m limit) is physically locked 10pm-8am. A beaches PSPO bans overnight camping, extended to Studland in 2022.

One further thread: in late 2024 the council proposed charging for overnight parking (5pm-9am) across the estate with a c. GBP50 annual overnight permit - aimed at cars, silent on motorhomes - then paused it in February 2025 pending a full parking review. The review's first proposals (July 2026) do not mention motorhomes or aires at all.
notes:
The mechanism matters: Dorset does not use PSPOs or camping byelaws against vans - it simply writes 'motorhomes not permitted 10pm to 8am' into the off-street order for each car park, so an overnight motorhome is a straightforward PCN under civil parking enforcement. Day access is genuinely good (31 car parks, dedicated bays at West Bay Road and Lodmoor), which makes the uniform night ban look like policy rather than accident: the council wants motorhome day-trip spend without the overnight.

Direction of travel is tightening. January 2025 added the night clause to more car parks, West Bay Station Yard went from GBP10-a-day motorhome parking to no-motorhomes signage, and the 2022 promise to investigate provision with CAMpRA has produced nothing visible by mid-2026. The paused overnight-charging scheme is worth watching: if resurrected post-review, it would monetise overnight car parking while the motorhome ban stays - the ban and the charge are separate instruments.

Small absurdity worth keeping: Charmouth Road multiuse car park in Lyme Regis publishes 24-hour (GBP33) and 7-day (GBP90) tariffs for over-6m vehicles while also stating no motorhomes 10pm-8am - the long tariffs are for coaches and lorries, not vans, and a van user reading the price board could easily be misled.
open_questions: Is the 10pm-8am motorhome exclusion in the base consolidation order for every motorhome-admitting car park, or only added progressively by amendment? Confirmed at six car parks; the full schedule needs the consolidated order text.
Status of the beaches camping PSPO after its 2022 three-year renewal - was it renewed again in 2025?
Whether the parking review (proposals to committee July 2026) will address motorhome provision or resurrect the paused overnight charging scheme.
Whether anything ever came of the 2022 discussions with CAMpRA about trial aires.
Whether Lulworth Cove car park (as opposed to Durdle Door) is also gated overnight.

sites.name: All Dorset Council car parks that admit motorhomes
sites.notes: 31 car parks admit motorhomes by day, with under-6m and over-6m tariffs, but the off-street order states 'motorhomes not permitted 10pm to 8am' car park by car park. Confirmed at Chesil, West Bay Road, Lodmoor, Charmouth Road, and added to Stour Meadows (Blandford) and Southill (Weymouth) by Amendment No. 3, in force 27 January 2025. Council position since June 2022: 'overnight sleeping is not permitted as car parks are not designed as campsites.'

sites.name: West Bay Road Car Park, West Bay (Bridport)
excludes_vehicle_types: motorhomes over 6m in standard bays (multiuse rates apply)
sites.search_hint: West Bay Road car park, West Bay, Bridport
sites.notes: The known West Bay pressure point. Dedicated motorhome bays (up to 6m at standard rates) by day, 438 spaces, but motorhomes not permitted 10pm-8am and the car park is physically locked overnight. The nearby Station Yard car park, which used to take motorhomes at GBP10 a day, is now signed no-motorhomes altogether (forum reports, 2024-25).
sites.geocode_precision: car park east of the harbour on West Bay Road

sites.name: Chesil Car Park, Portland
sites.search_hint: Chesil Beach car park, Portland Beach Road
sites.notes: The Chesil Beach pressure point. 616 spaces, open and charging 24 hours (the only Dorset Council car park not free overnight), with a GBP14-20 24-hour tariff - for cars. Motorhomes get day rates only and are not permitted 10pm-8am, so the 24-hour ticket is no route to an overnight stay in a van.
sites.geocode_precision: large car park behind Chesil Beach at Chiswell/Victoria Square

sites.name: Lodmoor Car Park, Weymouth
sites.search_hint: Lodmoor Country Park car park, Preston Beach Road, Weymouth
sites.notes: Weymouth's big seafront car park, 565 spaces with designated motorhome areas by day (under-6m up to GBP20.50 summer 24h-equivalent tariff), but motorhomes not permitted 10pm-8am. Weymouth is where the council's 2022 no-overnight-sleeping warning originated (Pavilion car park).
sites.geocode_precision: Lodmoor car park off Preston Beach Road

sites.name: Durdle Door Car Park (Lulworth Estate)
sites.search_hint: Durdle Door car park, West Lulworth
sites.notes: Private land (Lulworth Estate), not council. Gated 8am-9pm, ANPR-monitored, and the motorhome/minibus day tariff (GBP30) is itself printed 'NO OVERNIGHT SLEEPING'. Campervans pay the standard vehicle rate; cars towing caravans and oversized camping vehicles are refused at Lulworth Cove. The estate's answer to overnight demand is its own Durdle Door Holiday Park next to the car park.
sites.geocode_precision: clifftop car park beside Durdle Door Holiday Park

sites.name: Dorset beaches overnight camping PSPO (including Studland extension)
sites.notes: PSPOs renewed May 2022 for three years cover overnight camping on beaches, extended to Studland Beach, alongside fire/BBQ bans on open land. Aimed at fly camping (tents) rather than vehicles - the wording found does not mention motorhomes - but it closes off the beach itself. 2025 renewal not confirmed.
